title: RE3: Finding Refinement Relations with Relational Mapping Abstraction
problem: Manually constructing refinement relations between sequential circuits is tedious and error-prone, requiring deep domain knowledge and formal methods expertise, especially for post-transformation designs.
motivation: Refinement relations enable regression verification, assertion synthesis, and design space exploration; automating their discovery reduces manual effort and human error in design validation.
method: The algorithm automatically finds the mapping between two circuit designs—showing which states in one design correspond to states in the other—by checking whether they produce identical outputs over time (sequential equivalence checking). To make this mapping concise and understandable, it groups states that behave the same way (relational mapping abstraction). This automation eliminates the tedious manual mapping work that would normally require deep expertise in formal methods and hardware design.
key_novelty: Automatically discovering the refinement relation (state correspondence) between two circuit designs by grouping equivalent states—a technique called relational mapping abstraction—to create readable, automatically-generated mappings.
contributions: Rigorous and efficient sequential equivalence checking for non-cycle-accurate designs
Automatic discovery of concise, human-comprehensible refinement relations
Facilitates error detection and correction for LLM-generated RTL designs
Demonstrated applicability to complex design transformations
limitations: Scalability to very complex transformations and support for cycle-accurate models not discussed.
primary_theme: Automated refinement relation discovery for sequential equivalence checking
